This fall, the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts will spotlight the movement’s radical beginning and its evolution through subsequent generations of artists with “The Impressionist Revolution: Monet to Matisse from the Dallas Museum of Art,” opening Nov. 14. Along with abut 50 works from Dallas, the exhibition will feature 15 pieces from the VMFA’s collection that curators say enhance the telling of the Impressionists’ story. [...] One of the VMFA paintings in the show is “Lydia Seated on a Porch, Crocheting” by Mary Cassatt, an American artist who exhibited with the Impressionists. She played a significant role in introducing her fellow artists’ work to American collectors, Cunningham says, leading to more widespread acceptance of Impressionism.

Also among the exhibition’s highlights is a section of Monet’s work, including three of his water lily paintings spanning 1903 to 1917.
